title: Credit Notes and the Invoice Dispute Window on Corporate Travel Programmes
content:
A credit note is raised against the invoice line it corrects and never as a free-standing amount, so every credit points back to what it reverses. Credit control applies this to every correction on the Corporate Travel Programmes.

**The state the programme must stand in.** A credit note is raised only while the programme record stands at active, suspended or expired. The standing that answers this is the one the programme's own record shows for the programme being credited, read before the credit is raised; three standings permit a credit note and no other does.

**The dispute window.** A billing line is corrected on dispute only when frozen time is not after the moment the invoice carrying the disputed line was issued to the company plus the dispute window of the programme tier held. The moment the invoice was issued is the one the billing line's own record carries, correlated to the line by the invoice it was billed under; the window is the one published for the tier the company holds.

**Counting the window.** The dispute window is counted in whole calendar days from the day after the invoice date, weekends and public holidays included, and a dispute raised exactly on the closing day is still in time.

**A credit is not a payment.** A credit note never becomes a payment: it is applied against what the company owes, and a balance in the company's favour at closure is settled only after every open invoice has been cleared.

## The window counted out on a hypothetical invoice

Take a hypothetical invoice issued to a company whose tier carries a dispute window of 30 calendar days. Counting begins on the day after the invoice date, and every day counts, weekends and public holidays included.

| Day reached | Standing of a dispute raised that day |
| --- | --- |
| The invoice date itself | Inside the window; counting has not yet begun |
| Day 29 after the invoice date | Inside the window |
| Day 30 after the invoice date, the closing day | Still in time; the boundary day is in |
| Day 31 after the invoice date | The window has passed, and the line is not corrected on dispute |

The same counting on a tier whose window is 14 calendar days closes on day 14, and on a tier whose window is 90 calendar days on day 90. A weekend or a public holiday falling inside the window neither extends it nor is skipped over.

## Notes on a correction

- Every credit note is tied to the billing line it corrects. An amount the company would like credited with no line behind it is not a credit note under these rules.
- The date that starts the clock is the date the invoice carrying the disputed line was issued, taken from the record of that line, and not the date the company noticed the charge.
- A balance standing in the company's favour is applied against what the company owes; at closure it is settled only once every open invoice has been cleared.
